issue_context.title: LIFX Cloud integration ignores transition times from `scene.turn_on`
issue_context.body:
### The problem

If I call the `scene.turn_on` service and specify a transition time, the default saved in LIFX is used instead.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.4.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

lifx_cloud

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/lifx_cloud/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
service: scene.turn_on
target:
  entity_id:
    - scene.hygge_mode
data:
  transition: 180
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
No error messages or stack traces. I looked at the code for this integration and the transition time isn't being used.
```


### Additional information

https://api.developer.lifx.com/docs/activate-scene
comments: Not sure if related, seems like hue lights turn on are also not following the transition times. Off works fine though.

I'm working on a fix for the LIFX Cloud integration. The code I'm looking to fix won't help with the Hue lights. I'd be willing to look at that one too, but I don't have any Hue lights to test with. I'd recommend opening a separate issue.
I'm wondering if the activate scene service added transition recently and most of the light integrations haven't implemented it yet.

There hasn't been any activity on this issue recently. Due to the high number of incoming GitHub notifications, we have to clean some of the old issues, as many of them have already been resolved with the latest updates.
Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue has now been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.

review_comments: IMHO, the communication logic for the integration should be extracted into a separate library first (hosted on pypi).
I was trying to keep my change small to fix this bug, but I can pull in a library to do this. It'll replace most of the code in this integration 😂
I looked for a suitable pypi package, and didn't find an existing one that uses async io. Do I need to create one or are these changes okay?

We generally do not allow changes/new features to these integrations at this point, until they are extracted into a library (or use an existing one).

As for sync/async. Home Assistant can work with both.
